raw_response.blind_rationale:
1. SWiM Family Non-Fit Rationale (`none_nonfit`): Although the focal network exposures—ties to external partner organizations (`Number of partners`), two-step bridging ties (`Indirect reach`), and overlapping co-partner cliques (`Subgroup cohesion among partners`)—are thematically adjacent to SWiM Family B (external support, participation, and trust), excluding S1140 from Families A, B, and C as a reasoned non-fit is strongly justified because the dependent variable does not measure water or sanitation service access, coverage, continuity, quality, or affordability. Instead, it is a binary indicator of pre-construction competitive grant approval (`1` = secured RWSSP funding during the FY 2006/2007 planning phase; `0` = unfunded) prior to the development, implementation, and post-implementation phases. Synthesizing pre-construction grant-application win odds alongside realized household or community water service access outcomes in Family B would conflate upstream grant-seeking success with actual service delivery.

2. Scope Audit — Narrow Criterion 2 (`no_fails_narrow_c2_e03`) and Criterion 4 (`no_fails_c4_e04_or_e07`): S1140 should also be flagged for PI scope review on both criteria. First, under narrow Criterion 2 (`E03`), all 125 applicant communities face the exact same RWSSP institutional and regulatory rules; the three tested hypotheses examine informal, self-organizing ego-network topology metrics (count of organizations contacted quarterly or more, count of communities within two organizational steps, and percentage of copartner project overlap) without disaggregating regulatory contacts from banking, NGO, or partisan contacts (PDF p. 21, journal p. 327). Formal RWSSP grant-ranking criteria (expected household time savings, % marginalized villagers eligible for a 50% matching-cash subsidy, km distance to a bank eligible for a 50% transport subsidy, and beneficiary count) enter only as continuous community/proposal control variables rather than direct rule-intervention tests. Second, under Criterion 4 (`E04`), the author explicitly notes that the study examines only the planning phase and uses grant funding approval as the sole performance metric, leaving project implementation and actual water delivery unmeasured (PDF p. 21, journal p. 327).

raw_response.headline_estimate_summary: Table 3 (PDF p. 16, journal p. 322), Full Model maximum-likelihood logit regression predicting binary RWSSP grant funding approval in FY 2006/2007 (1 = funded [66/125], 0 = unfunded [59/125]; N = 125 communities; Huber-White robust SEs clustered across 37 UCINET hierarchical network clusters; Pseudo R2 = 0.43, Wald chi2 = 120.25, p < .01; no 95% CIs printed): (1) Number of partners (count of organizations contacted >= quarterly, range 1-16, mean 6.6, SD 3.16): log odds = 0.55, SE = 0.10, p < .01 (predicted funding probability rises from 0.02 at 1 partner with 0 reach to 0.38 at 7 partners and 0.99 at 16 partners, holding covariates at means, PDF p. 15); (2) Indirect reach (count of other communities within 2 organizational steps, range 0-38, mean 12.08, SD 11.09): log odds = 0.06, SE = 0.03, p < .05 (predicted probability at 1 partner rises from 0.02 at 0 reach to 0.044 at 12 and 0.31 at 38, PDF p. 16); (3) Subgroup cohesion among partners (mean % of copartners sharing projects, range 0-100, mean 15.86, SD 15.97): log odds = 0.02, SE = 0.01, p < .05 (predicted probability rises from 0.43 at 0% to 0.51 at 16% and 0.86 at 100%, PDF p. 16). Adjusted for RWSSP proposal-criteria controls and district dummies (vs Kavre; note PDF font renders minus signs as leading '2'): Time saving (hours/household) = 0.43 (SE = 0.15, p < .01), Social inclusion (% marginalized villagers) = 0.008 (SE printed as 0.0006, ns [likely typo for 0.006; Control-Only model = 0.002, SE = 0.007, ns]), Remoteness (km to bank) = -0.08 (SE = 0.04, p < .05), Project size (beneficiaries) = -0.001 (SE = 0.0009, p < .05), Makwanpur = 2.24 (SE = 0.75, p < .01), Sindhuli = -1.30 (SE = 0.49, p < .01), Sindhupalchowk = 1.39 (SE = 0.68, p < .05), Dhading = 1.75 (SE = 0.73, p < .05), Constant = -4.71 (SE = 1.03).
raw_response.study_design_and_sample: Cross-sectional observational network study combining retrospective on-site interviews of Water Supply and Sanitation User Committee (WSUC) officers (conducted July-October 2007) with Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Program (RWSSP) administrative records in Nepal. Unit of analysis: rural village community applying for a gravity-flow drinking water supply project in FY 2006/2007 across 5 districts in Nepal's Central Development Region (Kavre, Makwanpur, Sindhuli, Sindhupalchowk, and Dhading). Analytic sample: N = 125 applicant communities (exhaustive census of all 66 funded and 59 unfunded gravity-flow project applications in the 5 selected districts, representing ~74% of CDR projects and ~18% of RWSSP projects nationwide; average 683.90 beneficiaries per project).
